subject: Medisync request: 3-year forensics log retention & SIG/SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@medisync.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@medisync.com
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 3-year forensic log retention + SOC2/SIG evidence

Hi Connor,

Following our discovery call this morning, Medisync needs to confirm options for retaining request and audit logs for 3 years to support HIPAA-related forensics and incident response. Our security team is asking for the following evidence to complete our vendor assessment (SIG / CAIQ / SOC2 review):

- A copy or excerpt of Redwood's log retention policy and deletion procedure (what is retained, retention windows, deletion workflow).
- A sample of audit/log evidence showing retention metadata (timestamps, object lifecycle tags) — redacted is fine.
- SOC2 attestation details relevant to log retention and access controls (which report sections cover retention, location of auditor letter).
- SIG questionnaire answers specifically for data retention, legal hold, and chain-of-custody controls.

We realize this is longer than Redwood's default, so please advise if you support customer-specific retention exceptions or an addendum. Also let us know whether this is achievable in Hosted mode or whether we must move to Dedicated/Private.

Attached: Medisync_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (our updated SIG subset).

We'd like to close this path by next week if possible — can you confirm what evidence you can provide and any timeline?

Thanks,
Dana Lee
Sr. Security & Compliance
Medisync Health
(attachment: Medisync_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@medisync.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 3-year forensic log retention + SOC2/SIG evidence

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the questionnaire. I'm looping in Marissa (SE) and Hannah (Legal) to scope the technical and contract-side paths.

Quick summary up front: Redwood's Hosted offering has conservative default windows to balance cost and latency (request logs ~30 days, platform audit logs ~180 days). We do have two standard approaches for multi-year retention:

1) Private deployment / customer-managed storage — allows you to configure S3 lifecycle rules for 3-year retention and maintain chain-of-custody with your KMS/CMEK.
2) Dedicated + log-export add-on — we can export request/audit logs to a customer-managed bucket for a defined retention window (add-on pricing applies).

If neither option works, we can consider a time-bound exception for Hosted but that requires security approval and an addendum (we'll need to capture scope, retention SLA, cost delta, and whether deletion can be manual/legal-hold triggered).

What would help us move faster: please confirm which exact logs you need (NGINX/request logs, inference events, admin/audit trails), whether the retained logs will contain PHI or identifiers we should treat as sensitive, and whether you need immutable/append-only storage. I'll also attach a short Redwood summary of our standard retention controls so you have it for the SIG submission.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical call with Marissa + Medisync security this week — does Thursday 10am PT work?

Attached: redwood-log-retention-summary.pdf (high-level controls and default windows).

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-log-retention-summary.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@medisync.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 3-year forensic log retention + SOC2/SIG evidence

Hi Dana,

Technical details so we can map your SIG questions to concrete artifacts:

- "Request logs": we can provide HTTP access logs (timestamp, request-id, client-ip, path, response code) and inference event metadata (model_id, token_counts, request_id). In Hosted these are retained ~30 days; we can export on a schedule.
- "Audit trails": admin console actions (user-id, action, object, timestamp) are part of our platform audit logs (retained ~180 days for Hosted).
- Export options: scheduled export (daily/weekly) to a customer bucket; or continuous streaming to Kinesis/S3 for Dedicated/Private.
- Evidence artifacts we can supply: sample redacted log file with retention headers (e.g., S3 object lifecycle tags), S3 lifecycle policy examples, KMS key rotation logs (redacted), and a screenshot/export of our audit events retention configuration.

Note: for PHI-containing logs we recommend using Private with customer-managed keys (CMEK) so Medisync controls key rotation and access. We can prepare a redacted sample of retained logs (example: evidence_sample_logs_redacted.jsonl) and a short how-to for configuring immutable retention via your S3 provider.

Connor — happy to take the call and walk through details; Thursday 10am PT works for me.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: evidence_sample_logs_redacted.jsonl)

From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@medisync.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@medisync.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 11:37:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: 3-year forensic log retention + SOC2/SIG evidence

Connor / team —

Thanks for the options and the artifacts so far. To clarify Medisync's needs:

- We must retain request/transaction logs and admin/audit trails for 3 years to satisfy state-level regulations and our incident response policy.
- Chain-of-custody is required for any retained logs (evidence that objects were not tampered with).
- The logs will include PHI-linked identifiers in some cases, so encryption-at-rest and access controls are mandatory; ideally CMEK so Medisync can revoke access if necessary.

We also need the following documents for our SIG/SOC2 packet:
- SOC2 report reference (or auditor letter) that covers logging and retention controls. If you cannot share the full report, an auditor letter or statement referencing the relevant control sections is acceptable.
- Completed SIG v2 answers for data retention/legal hold sections.

I've attached a short spec showing the retention requirement and the audit/legal hold language (Medisync_Retention_Requirement_Spec.docx). This will be attached to our procurement/contract addendum.

Because this is a regulated requirement and there may be legal hold scenarios, we are asking Redwood to escalate to Security for an explicit exception path if Hosted cannot natively support CMEK-managed, immutable 3-year retention. Please confirm escalation owner and timeline.

Thanks,
Dana
(attachment: Medisync_Retention_Requirement_Spec.docx)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@medisync.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: 3-year forensic log retention + SOC2/SIG evidence

Dana — thanks for the clear spec. Summary of the path forward and action items:

1) Preferred technical solution (recommended): Private deployment with customer-managed S3 and CMEK. This gives you direct control over lifecycle (3-year immutable retention), chain-of-custody can be documented with S3 object lock + KMS access logs, and PHI separation is straightforward. Marissa will prepare a technical checklist for migration and a sample retention policy.

2) Alternative (faster): Dedicated environment + scheduled export to your S3 bucket. Redwood will export request and audit logs daily; we can include object lifecycle tags and retention metadata to support chain-of-custody. This is an add-on and will require a contract amendment.

3) Hosted exception (least preferred): We can evaluate a time-bound Hosted exception where Redwood stores a subset of logs longer, but this requires Security sign-off and a signed addendum with cost/release terms. Laura, can you confirm if Security can approve a Hosted exception for HS-98765 and what evidence they'd require?

Deliverables we'll provide this week: redacted log sample + S3 lifecycle example (done), SOC2 auditor letter reference (we will provide a dated statement referencing relevant controls), and populated SIG answers for the retention/legal-hold sections. I'll also attach a draft amendment to add the retention add-on and the basic cost delta for the Dedicated/export option for procurement review.

Next steps: Laura — please advise on Hosted exception feasibility and expected time to decision. Dana — can you confirm if Medisync prefers Private (CMEK) vs Dedicated+export so we can prioritize a contract path?

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(attachment: retention-exception-amendment-draft.pdf)
